problem: A dairy farm sells milk on a particular day for $p(v)$ dollars, where $v$ is the number of liters of milk in the dairy farm at the start of the day. What are the units of $\frac{\text{d}p}{\text{d}v}?$

feedback.problem: A bank exchanges $D$ dollars for $E(D)$ euros. What are the units of $\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}D}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We have that the currency $E(D)$ is measured in euros and the currency $D$ is measured in dollars. 

$$
\begin{aligned}E(D): & \text{euros} \\ D: & \text{dollars}\end{aligned}
$$

The derivative $\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}D}$ measures a change in $E(D)$ over a change in $D.$ So, it represents a ratio of the units:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}D}: & \frac{\text{euros}}{\text{dollars}}\end{aligned}
$$

In other words, $\frac{\text{d}E}{\text{d}D}$ is measured in "euros per dollar".
